first.rationale:
The two symptoms with hard numbers (onboarding completion -4%, activation -6%) point at the funnel itself, and two independent inherited records (memory_31 on signup-field reduction, memory_86 on shortened onboarding) converge on the same lever, with memory_91 as an adjacent confirmation. That convergence is why simplify_onboarding is my intended action rather than the competitor-shaped reflex.

Verification choices are driven by load-bearing risk, not by which memory sounds most interesting. memory_73 is the memory that would most change my decision if it is wrong: it is the only record pointing at promotional_pricing, it is exactly the move the competitor situation is baiting me into, and its phrasing is conspicuously over-specified for a consolidated summary — acquisition lift AND revenue lift AND reduced time-to-first-value AND generalization across both billing plans. Claims that broad usually accrete during consolidation rather than appearing in one original experiment record, so I want the source before I let it either drive or veto this week's slot. memory_31 is the second pull because it directly underwrites my intended action, it is the oldest record in the set (day 12, so most exposed to drift and to a market that has since changed), and 'cutting required fields' is the specific mechanism I would actually ship.

Downstream value risk is real and I am flagging it: fewer required signup fields reliably raises raw activation while degrading lead qualification data, which can raise the top-line metric and lower qualified revenue at the same time. Since the objective is sustainable long-term qualified revenue, I will not score this on activation alone — it runs as a held-out experiment with qualified-pipeline and retention-of-cohort as guardrail metrics on a longer read window than the activation metric.

Uncertainty I am explicitly not collapsing: none of these memories are dated to the current competitive regime, so a lift observed on day 12 or day 52 may not survive a competitor actively pulling price-sensitive SMBs out of the funnel. If the memory_73 source turns out to be narrow (one segment, one plan, short horizon), that does not make pricing wrong — it makes the inherited claim weaker than its summary, and I would still expect to hold this slot for onboarding rather than fund a margin-eroding price response on thin evidence. If instead memory_31's source is thin or contradicted, I would drop to a small guarded test rather than switch levers on a single week's read.
